text.p: French President Jacques Chirac hailed U.S. President Bill Clinton's re-election on Wednesday, saying it guaranteed France a friendly, clear-sighted, competent and generous U.S. partner towards the new millennium.

Chirac, in a message addressed "Mr President, My dear Bill", praised Clinton's "wise statesmanship" and said his victory was "joyful news." He added: "May I say that no one is more delighted than I am".

"Your presence at the White House will guarantee us an American partner who is friendly, clear-sighted, competent but also generous," Chirac, a conservative, said of Democrat Clinton's triumph over Republican Bob Dole.
"I am glad that it falls upon you to build the bridge to the 21st century that you envision for the United States of America," he said.
Chirac won a seven-year term in 1995, becoming the first leader of a major democracy elected to lead his country into the new millennium.

"Together, it will be our task to overcome the difficulties of the turn of the century, but also to prepare a peaceful future for our children. Together we must lead our societies toward the third millennium," he said.
Chirac, who once studied in the United States and speaks fluent English, is the most pro-American of modern French presidents.
"I know that with your re-election the close relations between our countries will become even closer," he told Clinton.

"I have often had occasion to appreciate your wise statesmanship, your vision of our common future, your keen sense of the Western community, but also the warmth, the simplicity, the humanity of your manner."
